## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Daḷhadhammajātaka* (Ja 409) is a canonical birth story found in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework, the Buddha related this story while dwelling in the Ghosita forest (Ghosikārāma) near Kosambī, occasioned by the mistreatment and neglect of Bhaddavatikā, the royal she-elephant of King Udena [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883].
In the story of the past, a monarch named Daḷhadhamma ruled in Benares, served by the Bodhisatta as his most trusted minister [Cowell 1897]. The king possessed a mighty she-elephant who had performed extraordinary services in her prime, travelling a hundred leagues in a day and executing royal errands, but upon growing old she was abandoned and deprived of her honours [Cowell 1897; UNDV Conference 2009]. Observing her neglected state, the Bodhisatta admonished the king with verses emphasizing the moral duty of gratefulness and reciprocal care [Anandajoti 2010; UNDV Conference 2009]. He warned that anyone who fails to acknowledge past benefactions will find no aid when misfortune strikes in the future [Anandajoti 2010]. Moved by the Bodhisatta’s counsel, the king restored the elephant's past privileges, practiced generosity and good deeds, and attained rebirth in heaven [Fausböll 1883; Cowell 1897]. In the birth identification (*samodhāna*), the she-elephant is identified as Bhaddavatikā, King Daḷhadhamma as Ānanda, and the wise minister as the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1883].
SuttaCentral records four modern translations across four languages [SuttaCentral]. In terms of text reuse, DharmaNexus aligns four Pali passages between this text and the third volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (longest match spanning segment ranges §3.4–7.4 to §3461–3471 with a 0.96 similarity score), while detecting no cross-language parallels with scores of 10 or greater [DharmaNexus].
